title: Build a pool of competing consumers

task.text: Several workers pull from one queue; each job goes to exactly one of them.
Implement `Worker` and `WorkerPool`. `Job`, `Job.STOP` and `JobHandler` are given and must not change.

items: `Worker(BlockingQueue<Job>, JobHandler)` is a `Runnable`: it blocks on the queue, calls the handler for each job, and returns when it takes `Job.STOP`.
A handler exception skips that job only. An interrupt ends the worker and keeps the interrupt flag.
`WorkerPool(int workers, JobHandler)` starts that many workers on one shared queue. `submit(Job)` enqueues.
`shutdown()` lets queued jobs finish, stops every worker with one `Job.STOP` each, and returns once they have ended.

checks.title: A worker stops at the poison pill
A failing job does not kill the worker
An interrupt ends an idle worker
Every job is handled exactly once
A busy worker never holds up a job
Waiting is done by the queue, not by sleeping
Workers share nothing mutable but the queue

hints.text: The queue is the only thing the workers share, and `take()` already makes an idle worker wait. Which single worker gets a job is the queue's decision, not yours.

`Worker.run` loops on `queue.take()` and returns on `Job.STOP`. `WorkerPool` owns the `LinkedBlockingQueue`, starts N threads running `Worker`, and in `shutdown` adds one `STOP` per worker then joins.
